## Excursion via Socaire: highland lagoons and the Atacama Salt Flat

[Socaire](/chile/place/socaire/) is a village southeast of [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) on the road into the highland part of Chile's desert. For travelers, it serves as a cultural stop and a lunch break between stages of a nature excursion. We offer **one excursion** visiting Socaire; it is a full-day group outing, not a standalone short walk around the village.

The [Atacama: Highland Lagoons, Socaire and Toconao excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-highland-lagoons-socaire-toconao-full-day/) combines several natural areas that differ markedly in elevation, landscapes and walking conditions. If lagoons and birds are your main interests, the trip introduces several types of high-altitude environment in one day.

## Order of visits

First come [Miscanti Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-miscanti/) and [Miñiques Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-miniques/). These high-altitude bodies of water lie beside volcanic slopes, with deep-blue water surrounded by dry plateaus. According to Chile Travel, the lagoons are above 4,100 m, so the visit requires preparation for altitude and attention to wellbeing.

After exploring the lagoons, travelers stop for lunch in Socaire. **Lunch is included** in the published excursion, as are admission tickets to the highland lagoons and Chaxa. The village offers a glimpse of life in a desert settlement, but the program does not promise a detailed architectural walking tour of Socaire itself.

The route then continues to the [Atacama Salt Flat](/chile/place/atacama-salt-flat/) and [Chaxa Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-chaxa/), where flamingos can be observed. Afterwards, the group travels to [Toconao](/chile/place/toconao/) with San Lucas Church and its bell tower. The return to San Pedro de Atacama completes a busy excursion day.

| Stage | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Miscanti and Miñiques | High-altitude lakes |
| Socaire | Lunch |
| Salt flat and Chaxa | Flamingos |
| Toconao | Church and bell tower |

## Preparing for altitude

Traveling from San Pedro de Atacama to the lagoons involves a substantial gain in elevation. Even if the excursion includes only short walks, **conditions at high altitude are very different from those in town**. Discuss acclimatization, your physical condition and any medical limitations before departure. A demanding physical activity immediately after arrival is not sensible.

Chile Travel recommends warm layers, sun protection and drinking water for this region. Strong sunshine, wind and marked temperature changes between morning and afternoon are possible at altitude. Footwear should be suitable for rocky sections and stops in protected natural areas.

To explore desert ecosystems separately or choose a shorter program, compare [Chile nature excursions](/interests/wildlife/tours/chile/) and the specific options around [Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Not every Atacama trip includes the highland lagoons.

## What is included and what must be agreed?

This is a **full-day group excursion** including lunch in Socaire and admission tickets to the lagoons and Chaxa. The guide language, starting time and conditions for a private booking cannot be inferred from that information and must be agreed for the selected date.

Flamingos are a natural attraction of Chaxa Lagoon. The itinerary includes the area, but the number of birds and distance from which they can be observed depend on nature and visitor rules. Watching takes place in accordance with the protected area's requirements.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions via Socaire

### Is Socaire the final destination?

No. After lunch in Socaire, the [current itinerary](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-highland-lagoons-socaire-toconao-full-day/) continues to the Atacama Salt Flat, Chaxa Lagoon and Toconao.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. Lunch in Socaire is included together with admission tickets to Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons and Chaxa.

### How high are the lagoons?

According to Chile's official tourism portal, Miscanti and Miñiques lie above 4,100 m. Planning the excursion requires attention to acclimatization and wellbeing.

### Can you see flamingos?

The excursion includes [Chaxa Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-chaxa/), known for flamingo watching. The number of birds seen cannot be guaranteed.

## Excursions to Tahai on Easter Island

[Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/) is a coastal archaeological complex on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), where ceremonial platforms with moai have been preserved and restored. One of its most recognizable features is Ko Te Riku, with restored eyes on the statue. Tahai shows how individual monuments relate to the coast and the traditions of the Rapa Nui people.

We include Tahai in several **short cultural excursions in the central part of the island**. They also pass through [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) and the [Puna Pau quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/), so the main differences concern guiding arrangements and additional stops. Our catalog does not contain a separate paid excursion devoted solely to Tahai.

## Three itineraries visiting Tahai

[Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-akivi-puna-pau-tahai/) is a private morning trip to three monuments. It begins with the seven moai at Ahu Akivi, continues to Puna Pau, where red volcanic stone was quarried for pukao topknots, and ends at Tahai. The Tahai complex includes its ceremonial platforms and Ko Te Riku.

[Ahu Akivi, Hanga Pukure, Puna Pau and Tahai](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/) is a **four-hour private excursion with an English-speaking guide**. Its distinguishing feature is an additional unrestored platform at [Hanga Pukure](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/). A Russian-speaking guide is listed as a possible service at an additional charge.

[Easter Island: Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-akivi-puna-pau-tahai-visit/) is another current option visiting the same principal archaeological sites, with Hanga Pukure also mentioned. Its private format and guide language have not been confirmed in advance, so they need clarification before booking.

| Program | Distinguishing feature |
|---|---|
| Three monuments | Private morning trip |
| With Hanga Pukure | 4 hours, English-speaking guide |
| Easter Island option | Similar geography |

The routes' similarity does not mean their prices, inclusions or guiding arrangements are identical. Before choosing, compare the detailed timing and confirm which additional services are actually included.

## Why Tahai is interesting after Puna Pau

At Puna Pau, visitors learn where the red stone used for pukao topknots came from. At Ahu Akivi, seven restored moai stand on a platform away from the shoreline. Tahai reveals another aspect of that history: a coastal ceremonial area with several ahu and restored features of the statues' appearance.

According to the Ma'u Henua community that manages the park, Tahai includes three restored platforms and traces of an ancient settlement. It is also known for sunset views, but **the morning excursions listed do not guarantee a visit at sunset**. The actual stop time depends on the chosen program.

## Rules at archaeological sites

Visits to archaeological sites in Rapa Nui National Park are subject to ticket and accredited-guide requirements. Park rules prohibit touching moai, leaving marked paths or moving stones. These restrictions also apply to short walking stops near ceremonial platforms.

If your trip includes several island excursions, agree on their order in advance: Rano Raraku and Orongo have special limits on repeat entry with a single ticket. Tahai itself can be part of a short introductory tour, with a longer route to other monuments left for another day.

Comfortable shoes, water and protection from sun and wind are useful. The island's outdoor sites are exposed, and even a short walk between viewpoints must respect the boundaries of protected areas.

## Frequently asked questions about Tahai excursions

### What other places are included with Tahai?

All three associated programs feature [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) and [Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/). Some options also include [Hanga Pukure](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/).

### Can you arrange to visit Tahai specifically at sunset?

Tahai is known for its evening views, but the listed excursions do not guarantee a sunset stop. That timing must be agreed separately.

### Which excursion includes a Russian-speaking guide?

The [four-hour private program](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/) normally specifies English, with a Russian-speaking guide available for an extra charge. The language for other options must be confirmed.

### Do national park rules apply?

Yes. Visitors to protected archaeological sites must follow marked paths, avoid touching monuments and comply with the park's ticket and guide arrangements.

## Excursion to San Lucas Church and the Toconao bell tower

[San Lucas Church and its bell tower](/chile/place/toconao-san-lucas-church-bell-tower/) stand in the Chilean village of [Toconao](/chile/place/toconao/) near the Atacama Salt Flat. The church and separate stone tower display local architecture that contrasts sharply with the highland lagoon landscapes. Both are part of Ada Tours' [Atacama: Highland Lagoons, Socaire and Toconao day excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-highland-lagoons-socaire-toconao-full-day/).

The church visit is the final cultural stop on a longer nature itinerary. We do not currently offer a separate excursion only to the church.

## What makes the architectural ensemble notable?

San Lucas Church and its freestanding bell tower are Toconao's principal architectural landmarks. Volcanic stone has long been widely used in local buildings. The tower has a stepped structure quite different from typical European bell towers.

Chile's National Monuments Council classifies the Toconao bell tower as a historic monument. It received that designation under Decree No. 5058 of 1951. The church and tower are connected by a shared square but remain two separate structures; seeing them together makes sense.

You can appreciate the exterior during the village stop. Access inside the church, attendance at a religious service or entry into the tower depends on local rules; permanently open access is not guaranteed.

## How the Atacama excursion reaches Toconao

The current [lagoon and Toconao excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-highland-lagoons-socaire-toconao-full-day/) first visits Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons. Lunch follows in Socaire, then the group explores the Atacama Salt Flat, Chaxa Lagoon and its flamingo habitat. Only after this nature itinerary does the route continue to Toconao to see the church and bell tower.

The contrast between nature and culture makes the journey varied. In the highlands, the main impressions are vast spaces, water and mountains. In Toconao, they are the village streets, stonework, square and local history.

The selected excursion includes admission tickets to the highland lagoons and Chaxa Lagoon, plus lunch in Socaire. These are inclusions for this particular day trip. No separate paid admission inside the church is promised.

## How an excursion to Toconao differs from visiting only the church

| Stop | What you learn |
|---|---|
| [Toconao](/chile/place/toconao/) | The village and local life |
| [San Lucas and its bell tower](/chile/place/toconao-san-lucas-church-bell-tower/) | Architecture and heritage |
| Atacama lagoons | Highland nature |

The village page explains Toconao's geography and character. Here, we focus on what visitors see in the square and why the stone tower is a protected monument. On the excursion, these elements form a single short cultural stop, not two separately charged activities.

As the full-day route covers several distant sites, time at the church is limited by the overall program. To study the architecture in detail or participate in the local church's activities, you would need to arrange extra time separately.

## Preparing for the trip

The route includes high-altitude areas with strong sunshine and significant temperature changes. Warm layers, sunscreen, drinking water and attention to altitude are important for the lagoons. Conditions are milder in Toconao, but the overall excursion remains long.

Allow some time to appreciate the historic structures from outside, and respect local rules when visiting a religious site. Do not assume guided access to interiors without separate confirmation.

## Frequently asked questions about San Lucas excursions

### Are the church and bell tower in the same place?

Yes. They stand near each other in Toconao, but are separate buildings within one architectural ensemble.

### Is this a standalone Ada Tours excursion?

We show the church and tower on the [Atacama lagoons and Toconao excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-highland-lagoons-socaire-toconao-full-day/). We do not currently offer a separate church-only excursion.

### Can you go inside the church?

That depends on local access arrangements. The itinerary confirms a visit to the site but does not promise unrestricted entry at any time.

## Toconao excursions: a village in the Atacama Desert

[Toconao](/chile/place/toconao/) is a small village near the Atacama Salt Flat, south of San Pedro de Atacama. Travelers visit it on excursions to the highland lagoons and natural sites of the desert. After open areas of mountains and saline lakes, they encounter local stone architecture and a village square.

One of our programs is the [Atacama: Highland Lagoons, Socaire and Toconao excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-highland-lagoons-socaire-toconao-full-day/). It takes a full day, with Toconao as a cultural stop after the main natural attractions.

## What to see in Toconao

The village's most recognizable landmark is [San Lucas Church and its separate bell tower](/chile/place/toconao-san-lucas-church-bell-tower/). Their stone architecture reflects local building traditions. The bell tower is recognized as a Chilean historic monument; exploring the ensemble shows what a settlement in one of the country's driest regions looks like.

Low buildings, streets and the square contrast noticeably with the lagoon landscapes. The stop appeals to travelers interested in both Atacama's natural scenery and its local culture. Access inside the church depends on its operating arrangements; the program does not promise entry to the interior.

## How the excursion visiting Toconao works

Our excursion includes the highland Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons, lunch in Socaire, the Atacama Salt Flat and Chaxa Lagoon within the Los Flamencos National Reserve. Travelers then reach Toconao to see San Lucas Church and its bell tower before returning to San Pedro de Atacama.

| Stage | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Highland lagoons | Blue lakes and mountains |
| Socaire | Lunch stop |
| Salt flat and Chaxa | Saline landscapes, birds |
| Toconao | Stone architecture |

The [Atacama excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-highland-lagoons-socaire-toconao-full-day/) includes admission to the lagoons and lunch in Socaire. These conditions should not automatically be assumed for other trips through Toconao.

## How much time to allow for the village

On the full-day excursion, Toconao is one of several stops. Traveling to and from the lagoons takes substantial time, so the program does not include a separate multi-day stay in the village.

If historic architecture and an unhurried stroll are your main interests, discuss a longer stop. If you primarily want to see the lagoons, visiting Toconao at the end adds variety without replacing the natural sites.

For an independent visit, consider the distance from San Pedro de Atacama, available transport and local opening hours. Short distances on a map do not necessarily reflect road conditions or the altitude of other sections of the route.

## Altitude, weather and safety

Toconao lies below the highland lagoons. However, this excursion climbs into areas above 4,000 meters, and those sections require special attention to health and acclimatization. Warm layers, water and sunscreen are useful for mountain stops.

If you struggle with altitude or plan to travel with children, discuss the whole route in advance, not only Toconao itself. A gentler alternative may be more suitable, without promising a safe outcome for every participant.

## Frequently asked questions about Toconao excursions

### Can you combine Toconao with Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons?

Yes. This combination is explicitly included in the [current Ada Tours itinerary](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-highland-lagoons-socaire-toconao-full-day/).

### Is a visit to San Lucas Church included?

Yes. The itinerary lists the church and bell tower. Entry into the buildings must be checked separately.

### Do you need acclimatization for this trip?

The route includes highland lagoons, so altitude deserves careful consideration. Toconao itself is lower, but that does not remove the altitude demands of the rest of the day.

lead: >-
  This 12-day tour spans Chile's contrasting regions: the Atacama Desert, high-altitude lagoons and geysers, Patagonia with Torres del Paine, and Easter Island. It is a busy itinerary with several domestic flights, group excursions and changes in elevation and climate. Discover how the days are divided, what to consider about the long distances and which expenses are not included.
---

## The Best of Chile in 12 Days: Atacama, Patagonia and Easter Island

**The main attraction of this 12-day tour is the chance to see three very different parts of Chile on one journey.** Travelers first explore [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and fly north to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The route then moves to Chilean Patagonia and [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). The final major excursion region is [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), where you discover monuments of the Rapa Nui culture.

This tour suits travelers comfortable with frequent changes of city, overnight location, natural conditions and flights. Northern desert plateaus, windy Patagonian lakes and an island in the Pacific require different clothing and approaches to physical effort. The program does not include an extended seaside holiday, although Anakena is visited on Rapa Nui.

Compared with the [10-day Chile and Easter Island tour](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/), this itinerary covers much more of mainland Chile. The 10-day program includes Valparaíso and the Maipo wine valley, while the 12-day journey focuses on Atacama and Patagonia. Your choice depends on whether an island with mainland additions or the natural landscapes of much of Chile are more appealing.

## Northern Chile: lunar landscapes, salt flats and highland lagoons

After a sightseeing day in Santiago, day 2 includes a flight to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This is the base for desert excursions. One of the region's best-known sites is [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/), where arid terrain and unusual rock formations are especially striking in the light of sunset. It is a sharp contrast with the coastal cities of central Chile.

On day 3, the route passes through the [Atacama Salt Flat](/chile/place/atacama-salt-flat/) and the highland Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons, as well as the villages of Toconao and Socaire. The desert is not uniform: bodies of water appear in mountain basins beside saline plains. Flamingos may be seen in some areas, but sightings and numbers depend on season and natural conditions.

Day 4 focuses on the [El Tatio geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) and Machuca. The altitude matters in practice: the excursion takes place in thin air, with substantial temperature changes between early morning and daytime. People with health conditions that make altitude risky should discuss participation with a doctor in advance. Even healthy travelers should avoid excessive exertion immediately after arrival and follow local guides' acclimatization advice.

**Atacama is not always hot.** Highland stops can be cold and windy, so clothing for the northern part of the journey must include warm layers and sun protection.

## Patagonia: Torres del Paine lakes and glacial landscapes

After the northern region, the journey moves to Puerto Natales. Day 5 includes a flight and transfer; day 6 features an excursion to [Torres del Paine National Park](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) and [Mylodon Cave](/chile/place/mylodon-cave/). This is one of the biggest changes of scenery in the entire journey.

Atacama is defined by dry plains, salt flats and volcanic landforms. Patagonia brings cold lakes, mountain ranges, damp winds and the traces of ancient glaciation. The excursion offers characteristic park panoramas, including lake areas around [Pehoé](/chile/place/lake-pehoe/). Exact viewpoints, however, depend on road conditions and the group's particular itinerary.

Mylodon Cave provides geological and paleontological context. It is known for finds associated with South American fauna that disappeared long ago. The day is rewarding for nature lovers who are not planning multi-day mountain trekking: the program includes a sightseeing excursion, not a complete hiking circuit through national park trails.

On day 7, the group returns to Santiago. This brings one of Chile's most famous scenic regions into a short journey, but without several free days in Patagonia. Exploring glaciers in depth, long trails or independent ascents requires a different route and more time.

## The final stage: Rapa Nui and the moai statues

A flight to [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/) is scheduled for day 8. The trip changes character again: after desert and Patagonia, the focus turns to the archaeology of Rapa Nui's Polynesian heritage.

On day 9, the excursion visits [Anakena](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) and the island's principal monuments. [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is known for the quarry where moai were carved from volcanic tuff. At [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), statues stand on a ceremonial platform. Together, these sites illustrate stages of carving, transporting and erecting the monumental figures.

Day 10 includes [Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/) and [Rano Kau](/chile/place/rano-kau-volcano/), followed by [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) and [Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/). Orongo is linked to Birdman ceremonial traditions; Ahu Akivi is one of the well-known restored platforms; and Puna Pau supplied red stone for the statue topknots. These visits explain why Rapa Nui's archaeological heritage cannot be reduced to a single photograph of its famous figures.

On day 11, the group returns to Santiago; on day 12, travelers head to the airport for their flight home. A possible vineyard visit after returning is described as optional, so a wine tour must not be treated as a compulsory part of the 12-day program.

## The itinerary in numbers: time spent in each region

| Days | Where the program takes place |
|---|---|
| 1 | Santiago |
| 2–4 | Atacama and Calama |
| 5–7 | Puerto Natales, Torres del Paine |
| 8–10 | Easter Island |
| 11–12 | Return and departure |

Several journeys between regions are by air. Before choosing travel dates, arrange connections and make sure available flights preserve the excursion sequence. International and domestic air tickets are excluded from the included services, so the tour price without flights cannot be treated as the final travel budget.

This itinerary is particularly sensitive to weather. In Atacama, altitude and early departures affect wellbeing; in Patagonia, wind can change the plans for a sightseeing day; reaching the remote island requires a separate buffer. When choosing, discuss both dates and the acceptable flexibility of the entire journey.

## Accommodation, guiding and expenses

The price includes hotel accommodation with breakfast, excursions with transport, a group guide, airport–hotel transfers, meals along the itinerary and admission tickets as stated in the program. Traveler assistance is available **24/7** throughout the journey.

Exclusions include **flights**, insurance, meals beyond those provided, tips and bank charges for certain payment methods. With several flights, ticket costs can significantly affect the total budget. Agree on dates and flight classes in advance, and check which expenses are charged per person, per room or according to the payment method.

The program uses **group excursions**. If you require a fully private journey or a Russian-speaking guide at every stage, neither can be inferred from a general promotional description: the format and language must be confirmed separately.

## Who should choose the whole country, and who should focus on one region?

The 12-day program suits travelers interested in nature and culture who are prepared for a fast pace. Patagonia here means a sightseeing day, and Atacama means several excursions from one base; these are not complete multi-day expeditions to each region.

If Easter Island is your main priority, see the [10-day itinerary including the Maipo Valley](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/) or a [short 6-day program](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/). To compare natural regions, explore [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and our [Nature section](/interests/nature/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Best of Chile 12-day tour

### Are flights between regions included?

No. Air tickets are listed as separately paid expenses. The itinerary includes several domestic flights, including to Easter Island, so dates and connections must be arranged in advance.

### Do you need mountain trekking experience?

The main itinerary includes sightseeing excursions, including a one-day visit to Torres del Paine. Multi-day mountain trekking is not included. However, the high-altitude Atacama areas require a separate assessment of altitude tolerance.

### When is the best time to see all three regions?

Atacama, Patagonia and Rapa Nui have different seasonal conditions. There is no single ideal month for all three; the choice depends on weather priorities and flight availability. A general comparison appears in our [Chile guide](/chile/).

### Will there be a separate wine tour?

A vineyard visit is mentioned as an optional possibility after returning from the island, not as a compulsory itinerary day. On the [10-day tour](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/), a Maipo Valley excursion is included in the program.

### Will we see moai statues?

Yes. The itinerary includes Rano Raraku, Ahu Tongariki, Ahu Akivi and other Rapa Nui monuments. The order of visits may depend on national park operations and local conditions.
